stories.headline: India orders Meta to remove paid ads promoting child sexual abuse
stories.summary: The Indian government has directed Meta to immediately remove advertisements and content on Instagram that promote or facilitate child sexual abuse material. The government issued a notice to Meta over content linked to child sexual exploitation and abuse in paid advertisements on Instagram. Meta, which also owns Facebook, has been ordered to disable such content and advertisements. The government has demanded an explanation from Meta within seven days on how such paid advertisements were allowed to appear on the platform. The move aims to curb the spread of child sexual abuse material on social media platforms. The government's directive is part of its efforts to ensure a safe online environment, particularly for children, and to hold social media companies accountable for the content hosted on their platforms. Meta is required to comply with the order immediately.

stories.headline: Compasses, not maps: China is building a different type of AI
stories.summary: China is developing a unique approach to artificial intelligence, focusing on systemic embedding and deployment across various sectors such as logistics, healthcare, finance, and urban management. This approach is reflected in the country's national policy, which treats AI as a capacity to be absorbed. Recently, Chinese companies have made significant progress in AI development, with Zhipu's GLM 5.2 model competing with American systems in capability, cost, and openness. Additionally, DeepSeek, a Chinese startup, has unveiled a preview version of its new model, promising to rival models from OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google. These advancements mark significant progress in the competition between Chinese and American AI labs, challenging assumptions about Chinese AI capabilities and demonstrating the country's growing presence in the global AI industry. China's AI development is driven by its national policy and is expected to continue growing.

stories.headline: Mandatory EasyPASS will hurt businesses, increase consumer prices - FABAG warns
stories.summary: The Federation of Associations of Broadcasters and Advertisers of the Galaxy (FABAG) warns that mandatory EasyPASS will negatively impact businesses and lead to increased consumer prices. This comes as households are still recovering from two years of high inflation. If businesses raise prices to offset the added costs of tariffs, shoppers may face further financial strain. According to the Yale Budget Lab, the average household is expected to pay an additional $2,400 this year due to tariffs imposed by Trump. Price hikes are anticipated for various products, including coffee, shoes, and appliances. The Consumer Price Index (CPI) will likely reflect these changes, measuring the impact on household inflation. As a result, consumers may face increased expenses, potentially exacerbating financial difficulties. The warning from FABAG highlights the potential consequences of mandatory EasyPASS on businesses and consumers alike.

stories.headline: Asia Property Awards: V-ZUG champions ‘Conscious Luxury’ in support of the 12th PropertyGuru Vietnam Property Awards
stories.summary: V-ZUG is supporting the 12th PropertyGuru Vietnam Property Awards, championing 'Conscious Luxury' in the region's property sector. The awards, established in 2005, are the most exclusive and prestigious real estate awards programme in Asia. At the 11th PropertyGuru Vietnam Property Awards, top Vietnamese developers were honored, with Kien A Corporation winning the top award for Best Developer and Best Mixed Use Developer. The winners included a range of developments, from condominiums and houses to resorts and industrial projects. The awards ceremony, held in HCM City on October 24, recognized 52 of Vietnam's top property developers. The PropertyGuru Asia Property Awards are considered the ultimate hallmark of excellence in the Asian property sector, with more information available at AsiaPropertyAwards.com.

stories.headline: China's Z.ai a challenger to OpenAI and Anthropic
stories.summary: Chinese artificial intelligence startup Z.ai is emerging as a challenger to OpenAI and Anthropic with its latest flagship model, GLM. The company has released its open-weight GLM-5.2 model and a new AI coding assistant, escalating its challenge to US leaders. Z.ai's model is considered to be as good as the currently available models from OpenAI and Anthropic, according to former US AI czar David Sacks. The release of GLM-5.2 comes after the US banned Anthropic from supplying its Fable 5 model, and its lifting of curbs on the company. Z.ai is part of a wave of powerful but inexpensive AI models from China that are challenging the industry's US leaders, including OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google. The development underscores China's growing competitiveness in the AI sector.

stories.headline: Google Unveils New AI Model to Rival ChatGPT
stories.summary: Google has unveiled its new AI model, Gemini, a chatbot designed to rival ChatGPT. Announced in 2023, Gemini is built on a large language model, trained on vast amounts of online data to generate responses to user prompts. Experts believe Gemini could be up to 10 times more powerful than GPT-4, the latest ChatGPT model. Gemini relies on neural networks, similar to ChatGPT, and is part of Google's efforts to join the conversational AI trend. The launch of Gemini follows the public release of ChatGPT by OpenAI in late November, which gained widespread popularity. Google's move is seen as an attempt to compete with OpenAI in the AI chatbot market. With Gemini, Google aims to provide a more powerful and capable AI model, potentially changing the landscape of conversational AI. The model's capabilities and features are expected to be further showcased in the coming days.

stories.headline: Meta Releases Groundbreaking Machine Learning Framework
stories.summary: Meta has released a groundbreaking machine learning framework, marking a significant shift towards transparency and open-source collaboration. The framework involves two main components: offline ML model learning and parameter tuning, utilizing time series data from production calls and simulations. This approach optimizes parameters and categorizes network types. The release is the result of several years of development and leverages cutting-edge machine learning. The framework is part of Meta's effort to promote open-source collaboration and transparency in AI research. Additionally, researchers have developed an active learning workflow to create a machine learning model for efficient prediction of complex phenomena. The release is expected to contribute to the advancement of AI technology and promote a culture of sharing and collaboration in the research community. The framework is now available, along with a how-to video and information on the people behind the technology.

stories.headline: Microsoft Invests Heavily in AI Research and Development
stories.summary: Microsoft is investing heavily in AI research and development, with a $190 billion investment in AI infrastructure and a separate $2.5 billion investment in a new group focused on assisting clients with AI implementations. The new group, Microsoft Frontier Co, will comprise 6,000 engineers and experts who will work with clients to design, deploy, and operate bespoke AI solutions. The investment aims to drive the adoption of AI in enterprises, with a focus on areas such as workflow automation, AI-assisted software development, and large-scale productivity optimization systems. The move signals a clear shift towards embedding AI across Microsoft's products and services, and is expected to drive long-term growth for the company. The investment will also support the development of Azure AI, as the company seeks to accelerate its growth in the AI market.
